subject: Re: Performance SLO / benchmark methodology exchange
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Performance SLOs and next steps

Priya / Amit — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the benchmark run:

Summary of requirements (from your side):
- Latency targets: P95 <= 250ms, P99 <= 500ms for short-form inference (<= 256 tokens); streaming tail acceptable for long responses up to 1s extra.
- Throughput: sustain 120 qps at 50 concurrent streams for text generation workloads.
- Concurrency: ability to maintain consistent latency under bursty traffic (burst to 300 concurrent connections for ~2 minutes).
- Streaming: client expects chunked responses with first-token latency <= 100ms ideally; server-side chunking OK.

What we (Redwood) proposed on the call:
- Run a two-phase benchmark: (1) functional reproducibility using your prompt set, (2) scale/load run to validate P95/P99 and throughput under sustained concurrency.
- Share a reproducible benchmark methodology (prompt sets, harness, measurement definitions) for your review.
- Provide a temporary test account + dedicated instance to run the benchmark in your region (us-west-2).

Concrete next steps:
1) Priya: share the canonical prompt set and any evaluation scripts you want included.
2) Redwood (Rishi + Logan): send benchmark methodology doc and the eval harness instructions.
3) Agree on exact measurement definitions (what counts as first-token, how we measure streaming latencies, how to compute p95/p99 over sessions).
4) Schedule benchmark run next week (we suggested Wed/Thu).

Attachments: we will send our methodology doc and our recommended harness config in the next email.

Thanks — Marissa

--

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Performance SLOs and next steps

Thanks Marissa — this matches our notes. A few clarifications and answers from our side:

- P95/P99 targets: correct as above. Note these are measured from our edge NAT to first-byte, so please include network delta when you share expected baselines.
- Streaming: for client UX we consider first-byte as critical. For partial tokens, we are ok if the first packet contains the first token(s); ideal first-byte <= 120ms for 90% of requests.
- Prompt sets: attached is our initial prompt set (edgefin_prompt_set_v1.json) and a short doc describing different user personas. This contains ~120 prompts across short, medium, and long response classes.
- Measurement definitions: see the attached PDF (edgefin_benchmark_defs.pdf) for our internal definitions — open to aligning on naming.

Questions for Redwood:
1) Do you have an eval harness we recommend for reproducibility?
2) Can Redwood run the benchmark from a dedicated instance in us-west-2 with isolated capacity?
3) For streaming, how will you report first-token vs incremental-chunk latencies in your run report?

We can make Wed (7/8) morning PST available for the run.

Thanks — Priya

--
Priya Shah
Head of AI Platform, EdgeFin

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 7 Jul 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Performance SLOs and next steps

Priya — great, thank you for the prompt set and defs. A few technical notes and what we'll provide on our side:

1) Eval harness: we will share Redwood's eval-harness instructions (attached: redwood_eval_harness_instructions.md). It uses an open harness (k6-based driver + custom client) that records per-session traces and token-level timings. We also support running the harness inside a container you can reproduce locally.

2) Measurement definitions (proposed):
- first_token_latency: time from request post to first byte received (ms).
- p95_first_token, p99_first_token calculated across successful sessions (exclude timeouts).
- full_response_latency: time from request post to final byte received (ms).
- throughput: successful requests per second averaged over a sustained 5-minute window.
- concurrency profile: we will report latency heatmaps by concurrency buckets (1-10, 11-50, 51-200, 200+).

3) Streaming: we'll instrument both first-token and chunk latency. For chunking we report median chunk-size and median inter-chunk gap; for client UX we will also report percentage of sessions where first_token_latency <= 120ms.

4) Reproducibility: we recommend running each prompt 5 times in randomized order, and publishing seed and harness config. We'll attach our harness config and a sample results template.

5) Dedicated instance: yes — Redwood can provision a dedicated instance in us-west-2 for the run and provide temporary credentials. We'll need an IP allowlist and the SRE contact (please confirm).

Action items from us (I): share harness instructions + recommended k6 script and a sample config. We will also prepare a baseline run on our side using your prompt set and share preliminary numbers before the joint run.

--

- SRE contact: please use sre@edgefin.com (Amit will triage IP allowlist).
- We'll accept the dedicated instance in us-west-2; please send the hostname and temporary creds when ready.
- Repro runs: we'll follow your recommendation (5 runs random order). We'll also attach an additional long-tail prompt set in case you want to stress streaming behavior.

I've attached the prompt set and defs in my earlier message. We'll upload larger files to the Drive folder and share when ready. For transparency, can Redwood also publish the raw harness output (CSV/JSON) and the script used so we can reproduce exactly?

One more ask: can you include token-level breakdowns for cost estimation (tokens requested vs tokens generated) in the final report? That will help our procurement team.

Best — Priya
